cct_range: HPS ~2000K (remaining stock) / LED mostly 3000K warm white (W zone <3300K); some 'modern business' zones may use 3300-5300K per plan
notes: CCT: Beijing's 15th Five-Year (2026-2030) urban lighting plan (published Sept 2025, loaded) says road lighting uses '3000K warm white as the main tone', with lower CCT on the Central Axis and historic areas and higher CCT allowed in modern business districts. Its colour-zoning table defines W = warm yellow <3300K and C = 3300-5300K. This is a plan and policy statement. The procurement pages I could read (DRC approval 京发改(审)〔2024〕365号, 2024-06-06; OPPLE lot-01 award, 2024-12-24, CNY 21.8M) put the fixture specs in attachments I could not see, so no fixture-level CCT was verified. STOCK: the central city has about 306,000 municipal road lamps, historically HPS plus metal halide. Phase 1 replaced about 141,500 HPS lamps with modular LED on 2,488 roads outside the 4th Ring (including the 4th Ring main and auxiliary roads) and some roads between the 3rd and 4th Rings. It started late 2024 and was reported complete in Jan 2026 (about 46% of central-city lamps). Phase 2 (about 55,000 lamps inside the 3rd Ring plus the Chang'an Ave and Central Axis extensions) launched 2025-12-15, with all work due by end-2026. Tencent News (Sept 2026) reports 2,146 HPS sets on Chang'an Ave and its extensions, the 2nd/3rd Rings and Qianmen already converted by Aug 2026, with CCT 'carefully designed' to keep a 'solemn, elegant' look (no K value given). LED SHARE: the plan says the central city is 'still mainly sodium lamps' with an energy-saving luminaire rate of only 60%, and sets a city-wide LED target of 60% to 90%. The 60% figure is a 2025 statement and it is unclear whether it includes Phase 1. By late 2026 central-city LED is probably well above 60% but unquantified. MEASURED: SDGSAT-1 first images (released 2021-12-20, thepaper) show the main urban area dominated by warm yellow HPS, and the sub-centre, Yizhuang, Daxing, Fangshan, Shijingshan and east Changping dominated by LED. Applied Energy 2023 SDGSAT-1 paper (S0306261923017191): Beijing >50% LED lighting in 2022. That is snippet-only (paywalled) and conflicts with the plan's 'mainly sodium' statement, so treat it as approximate. Suburban LEDs installed before 2024 (pre-plan) are likely cooler (4000K+), but this is not verified.

The Harbin urban-rural construction carbon-peaking plan (dated 2023-07-19, loaded via ccn.ac.cn repost) targets road-lighting LED/high-efficiency luminaire use of 90% or more by end-2024. It plans to retrofit 10,000 road lights in 2023 and another 10,000 in 2024. This is a target; I found no confirmation it was achieved. An ofweek article (2019-11-19) says 22,000 municipal streetlights were handed to the city investment company's streetlight office, which was replacing them with LED. The paragraph is under a Heilongjiang heading and appears to be Harbin, but the city attribution is not certain. Thepaper (June 2018): more than 20,000 streetlights inside the 2nd Ring, 17,000 on a smart control system (lamp type not stated). No CCT found in any source. The dominant tech is left as 'mixed' because the stock before the target date was below 90% LED by implication. Search budget ran out before procurement notices could be checked.

cct_range: local standard for new/retrofit LED: ~3000K, max 5000K (2024); legacy HPS ~2000K
notes: Shenyang Urban Management Law Enforcement Bureau reply to a CPPCC proposal (2024-08-09, loaded): urban streetlights are mainly LED (including 'energy-saving') and HPS, and LED plus energy-saving luminaires make up 65%. So the share is 65% as of 2024 and includes non-LED 'energy-saving' types. A four-year (2022-2025) programme is replacing energy-hungry luminaires, with 3,222 LED lamps on 133 streets done so far. That is a small number and suggests the remaining ~35% HPS persists. Local standard DB2101/T 0110-2024 (issued 2024-07-05, effective 2024-08-05, loaded), clause 6.4.2.2: LED road luminaire rated CCT 'should be about 3000K' and must not exceed 5000K. This applies to new works from Aug 2024 and does not describe the installed LED stock, whose CCT is undocumented. Earlier LEDs probably include 4000K+ units (era prior, unverified). The cct_k field is left blank on purpose.

There is little evidence. A Liaoning Dept of Housing & Construction item (Oct 2023, snippet only, page returned HTTP 473) reports 50 Dalian road-lighting construction projects completed and lit, with single-lamp control on new lights. Lamp type and CCT were not visible. The Dalian local standard DB2102/T 0099-2023 'Urban lighting technical specification' (effective 2024-01-29) prioritises LED, but its CCT clause was not visible in the 3-page preview. The Remote Sensing of Environment 2024 SDGSAT-1 China coastal-zone NTL type-classification paper (S0034425724001159) probably covers Dalian's coast. It was paywalled (403), so no Dalian numbers were extracted. The search budget ran out before a proper search.

Not researched: the session's WebSearch budget (200 calls, shared across agents) ran out before Jinan was reached. No evidence gathered, so the fields are left blank rather than guessed. Needs a follow-up search of 济南 城市照明/路灯 LED 改造 色温 and the Shandong procurement portal.

Not researched: the WebSearch budget ran out. The SDGSAT-1 coastal-zone paper (Remote Sensing of Environment 2024, https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/abs/pii/S0034425724001159) probably covers Qingdao, but it was paywalled and no city values were obtained. Needs follow-up.

Only one project-level item. ofweek (2019-11-19): the Shijiazhuang Urban Lighting Management Office retrofitted 12 streets (e.g. Jiantong St), replacing 1,161 sodium and induction lamps with LED. That is a single project, not city-wide, and no CCT was given. The WebSearch budget ran out before city-wide data or procurement notices could be found.
